title: introduce-tf-subnet-claim-controller-and-immutable-lease-module
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: Private installs have been facing drift and accidental subnet reuse during upgrades. This PR introduces a new Terraform module (modules/subnet-claim) plus a small reconcile helper to enforce immutable 'subnet claims' and a lease lifetime for GPU nodepool allocations. The goal is to make subnet assignments explicit, prevent silent re-use during rollbacks/upgrades, and provide a migration path for existing state. What this PR contains: 1) modules/subnet-claim: a TF module that creates a namespaced claim resource (TF state object) representing a leased CIDR + tags; the module exposes lifecycle rules to prevent deletion and supports an explicit 'relinquish' flag for safe teardown; 2) modules/immutable-lease: small helper module that wires a Dynamo-style lock (state-backed) plus IAM role that can be assumed by the installer reconciler; 3) modules/gpu-provisioner: updates to GPU nodepool TF to consume a subnet-claim id and attach a read-only binding rather than owning the subnet resource directly; 4) installer-reconcile binary (cmd/reconcile/main.go): an idempotent CLI used during upgrades that validates claims in state, acquires leases, and emits a human-readable plan for unsafe operations; 5) docs/upgrade-subnet-claim.md: migration and rollback steps for operators. Migration plan (in brief): run 'reconcile --dry-run' to enumerate claims and orphaned subnets; create claim objects for any existing nodepools using the --adopt flag; run terraform apply for modules/gpu-provisioner to switch ownership to claim id; cut over traffic to the new controller; monitor for lease expirations. Rollback plan: the 'reconcile' tool supports a --revert flag which releases claims created by adopt in a conservative way; TF lifecycle 'prevent_destroy' is the safety net to avoid accidental deletion. Tests & CI: unit tests for the reconcile CLI, terraform validate/checkov scan, and a focused e2e in the private-installer CI that provisions a single GPU nodepool using a leased subnet. Security: IAM bindings created by modules are least-privilege, and we add an audit role that allows only 'claim:read' to most service accounts. Backwards compatibility: existing installs continue to function; the migration is opt-in and can be performed incrementally. Rollout notes: staged rollout with a feature-flag in the installer; initial rollout to staging clusters for 2 weeks before production migration. Checklist: - [x] TF modules implemented and documented; - [x] reconcile CLI implemented and unit-tested; - [x] migrations documented; - [x] security review completed; - [x] CI green. Related: this PR complements prior state boundary work but avoids massive tfstate reshuffles by introducing claim objects that can be created without moving existing resources.

b7d4e22: implement immutable-lease module and IAM role policy
c3f9a01: wire gpu-provisioner to accept claim_id instead of subnet_id
d4b1f78: add reconcile CLI, dry-run and adopt logic
e5c2d90: docs: add upgrade-subnet-claim.md and migration checklist
f6a3b11: tests: unit tests for reconcile CLI and TF validate fixes
review_threads: Jonah Li: Overall this looks good but we need stronger guarantees around concurrent adopters. Suggested adding optimistic lock semantics to the lease module.
Priya Raman: Implemented compare-and-swap in lease.tf and added a TTL check in reconcile. See lease.tf commit b7d4e22.
Asha Patel: Please add an explicit documented remediation step if a claim is held by a zombie process; pointed to docs/upgrade-subnet-claim.md where we added 'force-release' guidance.
Miguel Ortega: CI e2e initially failed on a timing flake; rerun passed. Approving after e2e is stable.
Jonah Li: APPROVED after confirming idempotency with two concurrent reconcile runs in staging.
release_notes: Introduce subnet-claim and immutable-lease Terraform modules to enable non-destructive subnet allocations for GPU nodepools. Added reconcile CLI to migrate existing installs. Migration is opt-in and documented in docs/upgrade-subnet-claim.md.
